steps.text: The flickering lights of the ancient castle, the bloodied corpses of the teachers, the hollow wind in the darkness... Forgetting all of that was not difficult.
Until one day, when Lucian—who has by this time become an assassin—had a dream.
He's still in the old castle, still in that empty hall, sitting alone, singing under the lights, with all the former members of his troupe standing behind him—
As alive as ever.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Child, we cannot truly erase our pasts.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: There will always be traces of them.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Do you think I'm scared?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: No. I've simply finally confirmed that I've yet to fully tear out the ad-libbing you inserted into my life. In other words, you are still here.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: But you're correct: we cannot truly erase our pasts, and there will always be traces of them.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: So, to bring your story to an end, I've been walking the same path you once did, for all this time...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I traveled across the entire land!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Calais was a Gaulish border city.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: When the allied nations suddenly turned on them, Calais was thrown under siege. Yet thanks to its powerful cannons—and the general hailed as the 'Imperial Standard-Bearer'—Calais held fast for months.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The general stood atop the wall—refusing sleep, refusing rest, refusing to give ground. With their banner still flying high, even the weariest soldiers held the line.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Until the unthinkable happened, the general's most trusted lieutenant opened the gates, a clear act of betrayal.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: The Emperor of Gaul had given up on Calais, as by then its fate was sealed.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: The Imperial Standard-Bearer had refused to surrender out of honor, and the trusted lieutenant believed he ought to stand by his general. After all, they had already braved so many life-or-death situations together over the decades.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: But he knew that holding the line would only lead to more bloodshed—that the city was doomed to become a graveyard.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Perhaps that battle-worn soldier simply realized that although there was no perfect choice, there was a way that would allow him to atone for his sins.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: He persuaded the general, who had long since become exhausted, to take a ten minute break. Then he seized his opportunity to open the gate.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Before the allied forces could enter the city, he drove his sword through his own heart... That traitor ended up being the most tragic casualty of the war.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: But that is ancient history now, Lucian—so ancient that many of the details have long been lost to the river of time.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Victoria, Leithanien... I spent months traveling between more than a dozen cities across different nations, and at last, I found an aging Vanguard on the brink of death.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The guard had seen the towering flames of Calais with his own eyes. He had found a badge on the traitor's corpse—two faces turned away from each other, one smiling, the other weeping.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: We all know what that symbolizes, dear teacher.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Haha.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Then I suppose you made other discoveries as well?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Even earlier in Laterano...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Over 200 years ago, a brilliant cardinal was struck down by gun-knights in the plaza in front of the Basilica.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: He was intelligent and compassionate, known as 'the Sankta closest to the Lord.' At just thirty years old, he was already widely regarded as the Pope's heir apparent.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: But then, he changed. He grew radical, unyielding, unwieldy. He started preaching, rallying followers, and reaching out to foreign envoys, all in an attempt to check the Pope's authority.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: ...Until the situation deteriorated into a religious coup that threatened the entire city-state. The Pope was critically wounded, and the gun-knights were deployed. The would-be usurper became the only cardinal in the history of Laterano to die during a coup.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: No one knows what exactly happened to him... At some point, in one of the Ecclesia Requietum, he had a chance encounter with a passing Feline—but of course, that is hardly a lead worth chasing.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: It must have taken some effort for you to uncover all of this.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Indeed, it was quite troublesome.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: I merely offered that Sankta a bit of 'truth'—he was already terminally ill, you know.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Unlike the incompetent Pope, who knew only how to interpret scriptures, his own zealousness knew no bounds. But with limited time, he might not have been able to put his ideals into practice, to hear the church bells ring in the new era.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: But in truth, the moment the cardinal struck down the Pope, he came to his senses. He realized that death had never caught up with him after all.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: His sudden clarity only plunged him deeper into madness. Faced with the ruin he had wrought, did he choose to walk willingly into the gun-knights' sights?

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: A microcosm of political tragedy, from which many of the Troupe's plays took root.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Quite a pity, isn't it?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Iberia.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: It was during the glorious Golden Age... The lighthouses lit up an approaching ship—only for people to discover it carried nothing but whispering winds from the ocean depths. Ticket stubs stamped with the image of the twin faces were scattered across the deck, and they drifted along with the ship in silence.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The lost sailors sing—
Incite a young fowl, to pick the fruit of pain.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Amidst the spires of Leithanien, ancient Arts recorded the nobles' laments, and desperate cries.
Exile an infant, to arrive at joyful death.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: An encampment covered in thick snow.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Weeds walk their own path.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The city in the depths of the sands.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Through tears, falsehoods, and riddles.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: He leaves the bed of withered flowers.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: ...You are everywhere.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I followed the path you once walked. I crossed the lands, encountering all manner of people and unearthing all manner of secrets—until at last, buried in ancient tomes and tangled rumors, I uncovered your name.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: 'Tragodia'.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: However, the legendary Tragodia is a god, beloved by the people.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: He wears a crown of grapevines. He is both intoxicated and intoxicating. He bestows joy and grace. He greets the farmers as they bring in their yearly harvest, guiding them from wilderness to civilization through revelry and celebration.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: But the true god of wine is a deceitful caster, a performer, an ascetic, a schemer, a firebrand—a phantom drifting through the currents of history...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: A long-lived that defies definition.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: (Claps)

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Your perseverance astonishes me, child. Even more so than the painstaking devotion you once showed in your performances.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: And yet, when you look back at the path I've taken, shouldn't that be enough to affirm the purpose I've been chasing?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: As human affairs faded into obscurity, I found—and built—what I came to see as the ultimate vessel for beauty: the theater. I've lived long enough to see the very concept of 'theater' become obsolete.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: At last, after tasting both joy and sorrow, I came to understand the precise conditions under which the most fervent emotions bloom. I founded the Troupe—through which I've taught this knowledge to you.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Oh really?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: That contradicts what I've learned from my research. Hasn't death always walked by your side?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: That grand theory of yours—about death and destruction—was never the result of hard-won insight. You simply believed in it and saw beauty in it, and so did theater.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Let's set aside, for the moment, the brilliance or depravity of human nature that emerges in times of desperation—and turn to some more fundamental questions.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: From Laterano to Gaul, from Iberia to Sargon, from the old castle to this Catastrophe-stricken land—you've directed so many performances that shook the soul...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: So why have you allowed them to be lost to history?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You don't want them to be remembered?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You exalt the irrational and the unpredictable—so why must every story have the same ending: ruin?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Well, what do you think the answer is, child?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Tell me.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Because it makes everything and everyone unverifiable—both within the theater and beyond.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Because it grants you authority, lets you justify yourself, and turns your so-called 'beauty' into the only possible resolution?!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Steven...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Steven?!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: If you're still alive, say something!
...G-Greta?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: You really did lock yourself up in your office!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: What... what happened outside?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: It's too much to explain right now. In short, the entire plate is on a collision course with the Catastrophe, and everyone else has already evacuated to the power deck... Are you alright?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Y-Yeah, something's wrong... The ceiling came down on my leg—I can't move... Ngh—

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I'll rescue you!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Dammit! That broken column has sealed the door shut!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: It's really heavy! Just wait a moment! Stay with me! Keep talking!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Miss Stone, only now do I understand that I am in no way, shape, or form a genius.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: That 'god' came to see me.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: He hasn't abandoned me. He's shown me a new way of thinking. Actually, he's always been teaching me.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I like to think I make good use of my characters' deaths—of every desperate situation—to nourish my stories. I did try that, after all, in The Death of Lady Dupont. Why else would it be called that?

spans.text: I like to think I make good use of my characters' deaths—of every desperate situation—to nourish my stories. I did try that, after all, in
. Why else would it be called that?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Laura from five years ago, and now Dalton, Shelly, Michael, and Marion... Each of their deaths was steeped in drama: vivid, poignant, and all too real.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Those fragments are like autumn leaves—crimson as blood, and scattered everywhere. Each one is enough to stain the blank canvas of my mind with vivid color.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: But still—I can't write an ending that satisfies me! I still haven't figured out what kind of scene Lady Dupont's death ought to be!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: If death and destruction are the way of the god of theater—if they're the skills a true genius of the stage must master—well, I mean, I... I've never been able to learn them.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I'm just a *cough* worthless hack...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: For the love of Borgnine! How can you be so stupid?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Steven, the Script Auctions are anonymous. You know that, right?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Dalton, Abner—everyone in the crew has been shaped by what happened five years ago. I brought them together on purpose... But you, you were the one exception.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: When I approved the outline for the script, I had no idea it was written by you.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I simply felt, from the bottom of my heart, that the story of Lady Dupont—a woman trapped by her brother's lies and need for control, and tormented by the desires of three so-called suitors—was worth my vote of approval.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I knew she'd be a great protagonist for an amazing story, whether she lived or died.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I have never doubted my own vision.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Hey, say something! What are you getting all melodramatic for while I'm out here hauling rocks?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: So it turns out I just don't agree with...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: What are you saying?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Ugh! Saget! So it turns out I just don't agree with the 'god's' methods.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: There we are! I did it!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: This place is about to collapse! I'll help you! Come on!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Wait, wait, wait, Miss Stone.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: What now?
Greta helps hold Steven steady as they both come to a stop, and he looks to the side.
There is a wall, only half of it still standing. Faint remnants of vivid graffiti stand out harshly against the grimy, dim surroundings.
It is the giant promotional mural Tippi had painted for the crew, and by some stroke of luck, the title card remains unscathed amidst all the wind and flying debris—
The Death of Lady Dupont.
Steven raises a bloodstained arm and, with considerable effort, wipes away the first three words.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: My God...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: ...It's beautiful.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Not even the most imaginative set designer in Wrankwood could have created a scene like this. Who's to say that ending a film shoot under the shadow of a Catastrophe isn't, in fact, the most fitting conclusion of all?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: This isn't just a publicity stunt. I'm finding myself more and more impressed by Greta's resolve.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Alright, that's enough of that. Let's get back to the power deck. It's way too dangerous out here!

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Hey, Melanie, leading lady, where are you going? Have you gone mad?!

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Abner, you—all of you—never really believed this 'leading lady' could make a comeback with this film, did you?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: You don't even think we'll finish filming it...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Honestly, I feel the same. I mean, we don't even have the ending figured out yet, and this whole plate is about to collapse.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: But that doesn't mean you have to die for it, does it?
The Catastrophe is closing in.
The howling wind is nature's roar, its fury written across the face of the clouds.
But Melanie still walks forward to face it.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Who said I have a death wish?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Who says Lady Dupont has a death wish?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Who says Lady Dupont is meant to die under her brother's oppression, felled by the swords of the three Rockefellers, at the hands of those onlookers who sought to curse her, humiliate her, drive her out...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Must death be a symbol?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: She should instead, on a night no one could have foreseen, walk straight into a storm just as wild and chaotic as this one, leaving that prison of a castle behind.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: She shall not perish, because this storm is the chariot that will lead her to freedom!

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: You must have realized, Abner, that on my journey I've always regarded Marianne as my imaginary enemy, yes?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: But I know I'll never catch up to her.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: She was a true genius—born to inhabit any role she was given. Even fate itself seemed to orchestrate one final Catastrophe just so she could exit this business in a blaze of brilliance.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: And I'm nobody special.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: An ordinary woman from a small town, who traveled to Wrankwood and worked her way up role by role, film by film, for over a decade. Gaining experience and recognition...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: That's why I care so much about seniority, status, and etiquette. The aspects of film set culture that so many scoff at... Because that sort of recognition is the reward I deserve as an ordinary person.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: This land is quite cruel to ordinary people, Abner.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Marianne's retirement gave me the chance to step into the spotlight, but it took only a single slip-up for me to lose everything I'd gained along the way.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: My acting skills have fallen off a cliff. My reputation is a shambles. I've tried everything I could think of, but I just couldn't seem to get it back...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: It's ridiculous! I've never wanted to admit this, but it's true... If Marianne hadn't retired, I'd never have caught up to her!

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: And right this very moment, this Catastrophe is destroying the entire plate, along with my last hope.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: But couldn't you also say fate is smiling upon me?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: At least I finally have the courage... to let go of my inhibitions, the courage to...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: At least I finally mustered the courage to take this first leap.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Come to me, Lady Dupont. Come with Melanie Rutherford, and dance together with the Catastrophe...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Even if no one is filming us.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: What are you still doing here, Abner?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Check your camera. You didn't turn it on, did you?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: What, what do you mean?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: What if I'd gotten swept away by the storm? What if your camera had accidentally captured my death, just like before?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: The last thing I want is to belittle your work, and to force you to once again resent the tool of your trade.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: You know, Abner, I've always thought you were dumb.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Hey, what would you know?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: That footage you accidentally recorded back then at least stands as irrefutable evidence—ensuring that a girl named Laura wouldn't vanish from this land without a trace.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Although I couldn't say if that's enough meaning for it to meet your exacting standards.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Friedkin Kubrick! I am an idiot!

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: This 'dream-making machine' was only made in the first place because people wanted more eyes to see the land with.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: How long can you hold on, Melanie?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: ...I hope I don't break this thing.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Let's finish filming!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Can you see them? Can you hear them... those still fighting to survive the Catastrophe?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Nothing ever truly comes from nothing—not even the most wondrous of art. And it is never death that suddenly awakens the lost or steels the timid.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: They always had it in them.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: So, answer my question, Tragodia.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Are you attempting to remind me that death would simply end this story, this performance? That there would be nary a trace left after the curtains fall? That I will have, objectively speaking, escaped any and all scrutiny and criticism of my work?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: That I am a thin-skinned artist?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: You really did find an interesting angle, Lucian.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Perhaps what you say is right, but how are you going to change the ending that has already been written?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: That child, Tippi, really did adjust the path of the mobile plate, using only techniques she picked up from watching film reels.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: But the shift in its trajectory was insufficient. Nearly half the plate remains on a collision course with the storm.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Lucian, you faced a Catastrophe when you were young. You should know that one of that scale will destroy everything on this plate.
Lucian gently strokes the crystal on his throat.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I haven't sung since releasing the inhibitor.
Singing. It is Blood Diamond's song.

The song that once lit up countless stages, before dying out amidst the darkness of that old castle. Today, it echoes once more. The sound passes through cracks in the ruins and the Catastrophe itself, ringing clearly in everyone's ears.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Singing with such total devotion?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: It seems that dreams can also be used as barriers. This is the first time I've ever seen you use your Arts in reverse, Lucian.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Are you trying to protect everyone with the voice that once brought pain to yourself and disaster to others?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Are you trying to face this Catastrophe alone?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Alone? No. You're here with me.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Hold your scepter steady, Tragodia.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: From the moment I rose from that river and walked back to your side... From the moment I returned to the Troupe and stood before you once again...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I have only ever had one motivation.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: At the climax of every tragedy, there is always a fierce, cathartic battle—be it inside a palace, atop a tower... or beneath this ever-shifting sky.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Let us finish this drama, where the student kills the teacher!

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Haha! My favorite student! My best actor! Everything that is headed for destruction shall serve as your backdrop. I am so glad you can enjoy this moment!

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Even I can't help but be swept away in it! I've forgotten all other matters!

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: But you should know that killing a long-lived is meaningless.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You just told me that I found an interesting angle.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: But it's not interesting, far from it.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You aren't a thin-skinned artist. You've just been left with no other choice.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: It is not us who need to die, not the audience, not the common folk, bound by the laws of ordinary reality.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: It's you—Tragodia.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You've walked through history. You've founded the Troupe. You've created dreams from darkness. You've fed both me and Shalem with despair. You've drawn in lost souls, one after another, and lashed actor after actor...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You taught us to feel pain, to learn evil, to be stained with blood, to sing of destruction. You taught us to dress for the stage, to wear a mask in life, to believe in what you called rebirth.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You built the story and drew in the audience. You chose that Lateran cardinal, that Gaulish general, Whiteflower, Bladedance, Shadow, Dalton, Shelly, Moira...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You've chosen a million 'Lucians' with which to bring about death.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You exhausted its form, crafted its style, and perfected its meaning—

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Because it is all so far away from you.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: ...So far away.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Long lived—death is the one shore you will never reach. Director—death is the one performance you can never take part in. Tragodia—death is the one art you will never embody!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: All your aesthetics, your insights, your experiences—everything you pushed us to pursue has done nothing for you in the end.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I once thought this brought you joy, but your sorrow has always outweighed your sense of accomplishment!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: If you yourself are the theater, then your very existence is a paradox!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The ending is nigh, isn't it?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Do you feel resentful or helpless?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Do you find this funny or confusing?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Or have you simply ignored it?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Have you never felt the same pain that I have?
Tragodia is uncharacteristically silent, his eyes fixed on the face in front of him that is lost in emotion.
Lucian shouts loudly. The raging storm does not even distort his voice in the slightest. He sings, and chants—while the Originium crystals creep visibly along his neck.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Does it hurt, child?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Ngh—

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Yes. Of course it hurts.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: If you keep using your Arts without restraint, it will kill you, child.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Are you jealous?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Hahahaha.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Perhaps, but your performance really is moving.

Lucian responds to Tragodia with even greater fervor. His surging emotions give him newfound strength, and at last, he seizes the upper hand in their clash. In an instant, he plunges the scepter into Tragodia's torso.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Pain is my blade, and at last, I have driven it into the one who caused my pain in the first place—

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You!
The curtain must fall on every performance.
Cycles will not help shape our so-called 'destiny'.
Child, I've just gained new inspiration.
This story deserves to be continued.
The plate beneath their feet is swaying and shaking, but is starting to stabilize.
People start to poke their heads out from the ruins and look at the receding disaster. They can hardly believe the Catastrophe they have just experienced.
Hundreds of broken masks drop to the ground, as Tragodia slowly falls to his feet.
Lucian is sure that he has pierced Tragodia's heart and completed his grand, murderous drama. However, he also notices a change in himself.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: These clothes, this scepter, this crown...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Have you given me a new ad-libbing?
The silver-white hem of his robe flutters in the wind, brushed by grains of sand, yet spotless as ever. Lucian silently studies the elegant garment—
It is flamboyant and exquisite and fits him perfectly—as if it had been tailored just for him. He could walk into any festival or onto any stage in it, and it would suit him perfectly.
It is as if this is the Catastrophe's gift to him, his reward for slaying his teacher.
The theme of this murder was clearly 'betrayal', yet at the last moment it became a 'passing of the torch'?
Lucian is silent.
The fallen Tragodia has disappeared. Where he once lay, there is only blood, and his mask. The dark red carpet extends upward along the steps, without end.
This is the path he was meant to walk, and it is now free of all obstacles. These thoughts spring to Lucian's mind from nowhere.
So he climbs the stairs without lowering his head or looking back.
Just then, he hears Tragodia's voice.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Lucian, you are the finest actor in the land. You have honed your craft well, and you use your powers of reason to grasp hold of the mask of emotions.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: You know well my origins, so it should be clear to you that you have not ended me by merely killing me.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: You shouldn't pin your hopes on a scene that was once performed in an ancient castle.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Or is it that you were certain I would think this way—make this choice?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Haha. It's all so interesting.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Maybe you were right. Death is the one shore I will never reach, the one performance I can never take part in, and the one art I can never embody.

a.text: He leaves the bed of withered flowers.
He writes his epitaph into the stirring dust,

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: 'Death or destruction' is the greatest gift you could ever give your teacher.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: But have you considered that what you now reject—and what I've left behind—is only one of theater's countless possibilities, one of the many ways beauty can be defined?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: And therefore, that what you've just killed was but one of my thousands of existences?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Life rushes by, but the theater endures.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: The theater will never perish, and aesthetics will always change, so therefore I will always stand at the pinnacle of everything.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The theater cannot be killed—I can only redefine it, replace one theater with another, overthrow old aesthetics with new?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I can become the new one—the new you?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: If that is the only possible fate for the two of us—

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Then I accept it.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: You see, Lucian? Once again, we've entered into a tacit agreement. Haha!

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Continue forward. Climb to the highest point on the stage.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: You shall wear the crown of 'performance'. You shall wield the scepter of 'inspiration'. You shall wear the years of performing and being performed.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: This process will only add to your pain, but you must accept it.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: Child, you shall walk from here with both my blessing and my curse.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: I have fulfilled the promise I made to you when we first met: I will never be an obstacle to you... or an obstacle to theater.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: This is my final gift to you.

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: How much further can you walk?

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: What other answers can you come to—

steps.name: Tragodia
steps.text: 'Tragodia'.
Lucian does not answer, and the sound finally stops.
He stands at the top of the stairs. The storm is far away now, and blood trails behind him.
He loves this desolate scene, he loves the unformed Arts in his body, and he stretches out all his pain.
Then the new Tragodia sings his song—
